reason: The text contains regular human characters who possess dialogue, emotions, and opinions. Moses (מֹשֶׁה) has multiple lines of speech and expresses concern/doubt about his ability to communicate (describing himself as having 'uncircumcised lips'). The Israelites (בְּנֵֽי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל) are portrayed with emotional responses—they groan (וַיֵּאָנְח֧וּ), cry out (וַיִּזְעָ֑קוּ), and respond emotionally to their servitude. Aaron (אַהֲרֹ֖ן) is depicted as an agent with actions and will speak. Pharaoh is characterized with emotional/volitional states (his heart is hardened—וַיֶּחֱזַק֙ לֵ֣ב פַּרְעֹ֔ה). These represent regular human beings, not divine figures, who are given voice and emotional depth in the narrative.
